recipes.purpose: Show a true two-period change when the values cannot be expressed more clearly as one non-negative actual value against a prior or reference benchmark.
recipes.data: Exactly 2 labeled numeric values with measure.quantity, matching scope, and explicit periods. For two positive level values, prefer comparison.benchmark-gap with the later/current value as value and the earlier/reference value as benchmark.
bestFor: native rates or indexes where benchmark-gap level semantics do not apply

recipes.purpose: Compare actual, expected, target, or alternative values of one named quantity for one shared scope and period. Do not flatten repeated category/time pairs into separate scenario bars.
recipes.data: 3 to 5 independent labeled numeric values with measure.quantity and matching scope and period. Two generic bars are invalid even with supporting copy or a derived total. A defensible two-value relationship must use a relationship-specific recipe such as comparison.benchmark-gap, comparison.change, comparison.diverging, or timeline.duration; otherwise enrich, merge, or omit it. Two categories with earlier/later values should use comparison.benchmark-gap; three or more paired categories should use comparison.dumbbell. Give the current, prior, or reference level tone neutral and the alternatives semantic tones: with exactly one neutral item the renderer rules that level across the chart and labels each alternative with its distance from it.

recipes.purpose: Compare positive and negative changes in one named quantity for one shared scope and period.
recipes.data: 2 to 10 labeled numeric changes with measure.quantity and matching scope and period; values may be positive or negative.

recipes.purpose: Show exact values, min-max intervals, and thresholds for one named quantity on one scale.
recipes.data: 1 to 8 items with value or low/high fields, measure.quantity, and matching scope and period. A single interval requires a visible benchmark or reference that supplies the total or threshold scale and is invalid when visualEvidenceAudit contains three or more named comparable observations. When the finding is a threshold breach, the threshold itself must remain visible as a reference, benchmark, or threshold mark; before/after values do not substitute for it.

recipes.purpose: Show one non-negative actual or current level against a meaningful benchmark. Use the default gap relation when the distance to the benchmark is the story; use benchmarkRelation=consumed-share when the actual/adverse amount itself is being emphasized as a share of the larger benchmark.
recipes.data: 1 to 6 labeled items with an underlying actual/current value and a benchmark/reference value measuring the same quantity in the same unit, plus matching scope and period. gapDisplayValue must describe the arithmetic difference or remaining benchmark amount, never a ratio, per-unit equivalence, or cross-unit conversion. For consumed-share, value must not exceed benchmark; the actual segment receives the semantic tone and the unused remainder stays neutral. For ordinary gaps, gapTone may independently encode the meaning or severity of the gap segment instead of inheriting the main item tone. Use one item whenever two positive levels can be read naturally as actual/current versus benchmark/prior.

recipes.purpose: Show the concentration or pattern of one numeric measure across two categorical dimensions without flattening the cross-tab into a long ranking.
recipes.data: A complete 2×2 to 6×6 rectangular cross-tab. data[].label is the row category, data[].column is the column category, and every cell carries one finite value with the same measure.quantity, scope, and period. Every row-column combination must appear exactly once. Cell values are directly labeled and color uses one renderer-owned sequential quantitative ramp; per-cell semantic tones, sparse matrices, hidden labels, logarithmic color, and arbitrary sorting are rejected.

recipes.purpose: Visualize two source-supported causal drivers converging on a different outcome without forcing them onto a shared axis.
recipes.data: Exactly 3 items: two relationshipRole driver items and one outcome item, all with distinct real-world quantities. relationship.formula must state the source-supported mechanism. Directional mode additionally requires mechanism evidence that explicitly links the plotted outcome to at least one plotted driver; chronology or adjacent facts do not justify causal connectors. Every item needs a value or range, direction, displayValue, quantity, scope, and period. Repeated prices, repeated volumes, and the same measure at different dates must use change, scenarios, dumbbell, or trend geometry. Each item is drawn on its own local quantitative signal; the two driver connectors meet and continue briefly toward the outcome in the same connector color, and connector width encodes no magnitude.

recipes.purpose: Compare two values for several categories while preserving the direction and size of every category-level change.
recipes.data: 3 to 10 labeled items with value and benchmark in one unit, plus matching quantity, scope, and period. benchmark is the earlier or reference value; value is the later or actual value. Different categories may have different absolute levels; what must remain comparable is each category's own earlier-versus-later pair in the same unit and basis.
bestFor: target versus actual across several categories

recipes.purpose: Compare one quantity across categories for two to four named series (a cross-tab), or show two or three related measures side by side for the same categories. Use it instead of flattening a cross-tab into compound labels such as "A · B" in a ranking, scenario, or scatter chart.
recipes.data: 2 to 48 items. data[].label is the category (2 to 10, authored order is kept), data[].group is the series (2 to 4, omit for a single series), and value is the non-negative level. Missing category/series combinations are allowed and simply leave a gap. Optional data[].detail is a short caption (24 characters or fewer) drawn under a column or inside a bar, such as the loan size behind a payment; optional data[].annotation is a short muted note beside the value, such as "2.6× Moscow Region". Use panels (2 or 3, each with id, title, and a measure override) when the same categories and series carry different quantities, such as an interest rate and a loan limit; every item then names its panel. Without panels, references draw labeled benchmark lines (for example the payment before a policy change) across the shared axis. Set options.seriesScale to sequential when the series are ordered levels of one quantity (loan sizes, years); keep categorical for unordered groups such as regions. Orientation is renderer-owned: short category labels become columns and longer names become horizontal bars.
bestFor: policy terms by group and tier
before/after benchmarks across several categories and options
the same budget across several markets and amounts
two related measures for the same categories

recipes.purpose: Compare 3 to 8 positive magnitudes by proportional square area when physical footprint, capacity, land, floor area, or another inherently spatial size is the intuitive comparison.
recipes.data: 3 to 8 positive labeled numeric values with one shared quantity, scope, period, and linear zero-based measure. Square side length is proportional to the square root of value so visible area is proportional to magnitude.
bestFor: other physically spatial size comparisons; not shares or arbitrary scores

recipes.purpose: Show the relationship between two distinct quantitative variables across the same observations.
recipes.data: 4 to 12 labeled observations. data[].xValue is measured by xMeasure and data[].value is measured by measure. Both axes are linear and independently scaled; point position encodes the two quantities and direct labels preserve observation identity. No regression line, bubble size, or third color variable is inferred by the renderer.
bestFor: price versus demand across comparable entities
other paired numeric relationships where both variables are observed for every labeled item

recipes.purpose: Show a sequence over time.
recipes.data: 3 to 366 ordered labeled numeric values; 5 or more preferred. Dense daily series are supported when the date sequence itself is analytically useful. To compare 2 to 6 aligned series on one shared scale, repeat the same ordered labels for each series and identify every item with data[].group; each series may contain up to 366 observations and the flattened grouped dataset may contain at most 732 items. Grouped trends require no direct value labels and normally require a visible legend. For two or three aligned grouped series, options.independentYAxes may be set true when the editorial intent explicitly requires separate cumulative scales; the renderer assigns the first axis left and additional axes right, colors each axis to its line, and the colored axis titles may replace the legend. Set options.showPoints false when the line shape should stand alone without point markers. In a single series, an item may carry low and high beside value to draw its reported range as a bar behind the line; value is the plotted midpoint and displayValue states the range. Points are solid, nothing is filled under the line, and the renderer adds no automatic change label; an authored data[].annotation is the only note beside a point. A 3–4 point sequence of small exact counts or only two distinct count levels requires an independent same-unit denominator/portfolio benchmark or richer quantitative anchor; do not draw a line merely to visualize a few self-evident integers.
recipes.events: Optional. Up to two dated context events drawn as vertical marker lines, each anchored with afterLabel to the plotted period it follows. Use for an external event that changes interpretation of the series, never for a value that belongs in data.

recipes.purpose: Show how an additive category mix changes across ordered periods while preserving the monthly or period total.
recipes.data: 3 to 24 ordered periods. Each period carries 2 to 15 non-negative segments with the same category labels and order. Zero-valued categories are retained so colors and stack positions remain stable across time.
recipes.events: Optional. Up to two dated context events drawn as vertical marker lines, each anchored with afterLabel to the plotted period it follows. Use for an external event that changes interpretation of the series, never for a value that belongs in data.

recipes.purpose: Show dated policy, restriction, outage, contract, or operational intervals on a common calendar.
recipes.data: 2 to 8 labeled intervals with ISO start and end dates, or exact duration plus durationUnit when all intervals share timeline.anchorDate. Tone controls the interval color; displayValue names the duration.

recipes.purpose: Show parts of a whole when the shape of the composition matters.
recipes.data: 2 to 6 positive labeled numeric values.

recipes.purpose: Show exact parts of one total in a compact horizontal composition when the mix itself is the finding.
recipes.data: 2 to 6 positive labeled numeric values. Do not use a single hypothetical split when the source provides a meaningful policy, target, prior, or alternative share against the same tangible total; in that case prefer shared-total benchmark geometry.

recipes.purpose: Compare the same additive components across two or more periods, entities, or scenarios while keeping every group on one common zero-based scale.
recipes.data: 2 to 8 labeled groups. Each group contains 2 to 6 non-negative segments with the same labels and order. Segment values are additive levels in one shared unit. Group totals are encoded by full bar length; do not add a derived total as a separate series row. Label placement is family-coherent: if any segment cannot fit an internal label, all segment labels move outside and directly identify the segments with semantic text color, replacing the legend.
bestFor: same-component mixes where both component size and group total matter

recipes.purpose: Compare exact positive additive components of one reported total with every component seated at zero and the total shown as a numeric reference.
recipes.data: 2 to 6 positive labeled component values with one shared quantity, scope, and period. Exactly one numeric reference must equal the reported total within display precision. With exactly two components, add an independent same-scale benchmark or denominator beyond that derived sum; otherwise recover a third component, use another recipe, merge, or omit. Do not include the total as a redundant data row.
bestFor: budget components where component magnitude matters

recipes.purpose: Explain how an existing balance or level moves through exact positive and negative changes into a reported ending amount.
recipes.data: 2 to 8 ordered items with role start, change, subtotal, or end; every item also needs reported valueStatus, period, and scope, and the values must reconcile. Do not use waterfall when the intermediate values are simply positive components of one total; use composition.components so every component starts at zero.
bestFor: balance movements with genuine increases and decreases

recipes.purpose: Rank categories where labels need horizontal space.
recipes.data: 3 to 100 labeled numeric values. For a finite categorical domain, include every materially relevant non-empty category by default rather than silently truncating to a top-N subset. Dense rankings expand vertically and retain per-bar numeric labels. Bars share one color so length carries the comparison; explicit tones mark semantic status, and a ranking-focus story highlights the leading bar.

recipes.purpose: Show a geographic breakdown across named continental administrative regions. All reported regions can remain highlighted while callout cards are reserved for the most informative locations.
recipes.data: One item per reported regional observation, up to the region-set size. Each item needs regionId or regionIds plus status, tone, value, or concise evidence. At most 12 items may render callout cards; set data[].callout to none for fill-only highlights that should remain on the map without a box.

composableFeatures.purpose: Add a separate analyst, author, team, or public-account attribution, optionally linked, without conflating it with the underlying source.
List up to three further publications, each optionally linked, after the primary source when the chart combines evidence from several articles or datasets.
Show a right-aligned byline in the footer, such as analysisBy for the analyst or account that produced the chart.
Add one short footnote (eligibility rule, derivation, or caveat). Standard charts center it in the footer between the source and the byline; maps show it below the map.
Add target, average, legal limit, prior norm, or other numeric reference lines without changing recipe.
Attach one short explanatory note to a specific data point or stage.

Use logarithmic scale only for genuinely multiplicative comparisons across orders of magnitude. Never use it when the point is that an amount is a small fraction of a benchmark or denominator; preserve that proportional gap with a linear scale and period-normalize an oversized monthly or annual flow benchmark when needed.

Add up to four genuinely secondary contextual facts after a primary visual that already satisfies its recipe-specific evidence gate. Supporting facts cannot rescue two generic bars or become the chart.
Expose the tangible numerator and denominator behind a share or ratio, or the total population and affected count behind a risk estimate.
